stem: The businessowners policy is described as:
options: A monoline property policy for large businesses
A complete package policy with few optional coverages for certain small and medium sized businesses
explanation: The BOP is a complete package policy with few optional coverages, meant for certain small and medium sized businesses, with one property coverage form written on a special or open peril basis.

stem: Which business is INELIGIBLE for a businessowners policy?
explanation: Ineligible businesses include bars, grills and restaurants, condo associations other than office or residential, contractors, places of amusement, wholesalers, financial institutions, and auto dealers or auto repair and servicing.

stem: The maximum gross receipts allowed for a businessowners policy is:
explanation: The maximums allowable are 6 stories, 100,000 square feet with not more than 25,000 square feet in any one business, and $3,000,000 in gross receipts.

stem: The building height and area maximums for a businessowners policy are:
options: 3 stories and 50,000 square feet in any one business
10 stories and 250,000 square feet with no per business limit
6 stories and 100,000 square feet, with no more than 25,000 square feet in any one business
explanation: The maximums allowable are six stories, one hundred thousand square feet, not more than twenty-five thousand square feet in any one business, and three million dollars in gross receipts.

stem: Peak season coverage under the BOP provides:
options: A 25 percent automatic increase during seasonal periods at no additional charge
A 10 percent increase requiring an additional premium
explanation: Peak season coverage provides a twenty-five percent automatic increase during seasonal periods at no additional charge.

stem: Business income coverage under the BOP is written as:
options: A limit equal to 12 months of gross receipts
An unlimited dollar amount that expires at the expected business continuation date but no more than 12 months
A limit of 30 percent of the building limit
explanation: Business income coverage is an unlimited dollar amount that expires at the expected business continuation date but no more than 12 months.

stem: If a BOP-covered building is vacant over 60 days, what happens?
options: Only wind and hail remain covered
There is no coverage for theft, vandalism or sprinkler leakage, and all other losses are reduced by 15 percent
explanation: If the building is vacant over 60 days, there is no coverage for theft, vandalism or sprinkler leakage, and all other losses are reduced by 15 percent.

stem: The honesty clause in a BOP reporting form:
options: Rewards accurate reporting with a premium credit
Penalizes those who under report, reducing the claim payment by the percentage of under report
explanation: The honesty clause will penalize those who under report, and in the event of a loss the claim payment will be reduced by the percentage of under report.

stem: Extra expense insurance indemnifies the insured for:
options: The cost to rebuild the building
Lost sales for the full restoration period
Expenses incurred when the business temporarily relocates to prevent loss of income because the building was damaged by a covered peril
explanation: Extra expense insurance indemnifies the insured for expenses incurred when the business temporarily relocates to another location to prevent loss of income because the building has been damaged by a covered peril.

stem: Fire legal liability under BOP Section II is written at:
explanation: Section II business liability includes fire legal liability at three hundred thousand dollars per occurrence, described as lawsuit protection.

stem: Premises and operations coverage responds to injury or damage:
options: Only from products sold by the business
Only after the work is completed
Occurring at the place of business or arising from the type of business conducted
explanation: Premises and operations covers bodily injury or property damage occurring at the place of business or from the type of business conducted, and the operations exposure can be on or off the premises but primarily off.

stem: Advertising injury and personal injury coverage:
options: Cover bodily injury but not property damage
Do not cover bodily injury or property damage
Cover property damage but not bodily injury
Cover both bodily injury and property damage
explanation: Advertising injury and personal injury do not cover bodily injury or property damage; they respond to offense-type exposures such as defamation.

stem: Which offense belongs to advertising injury rather than personal injury?
options: Wrongful eviction from a room or dwelling
explanation: Advertising injury includes misappropriation of advertising ideas or style and infringement of title or slogan, while personal injury adds wrongful entry or eviction and false arrest, detention, imprisonment and malicious prosecution.

stem: Fire legal liability covers:
options: All damage to the entire building
Damage to the insured's own building
Damage caused by a fire that starts off the premises
Damage caused by an insured to that part of a building leased or rented, if it should burn or explode
explanation: Fire legal, or tenant liability, covers damage caused by an insured to that part of any building leased or rented if it should burn, explode or suffer other stated perils, with the rest of the building covered by the premises liability coverage.

stem: Medical payments to others under the CGL:
options: Pays medical bills of others regardless of negligence to discourage lawsuits, for up to 1 year from the occurrence
Pays only after the insured is found negligent
Applies to employees injured on the job
Is payable for 3 years after the occurrence
explanation: Medical payments to others pays medical bills of others regardless of negligence to discourage lawsuits, with a per person basic minimum limit payable for up to 1 year from the occurrence.

stem: Product liability does NOT cover:
options: Bodily injury caused by a defective product
Property damage caused by a defective product
Damage to the product itself or the cost to recall the defective product
Injury occurring off the business premises
explanation: Product liability covers BI/PD caused by a defective product but does not cover damage to the product itself or the cost to recall the defective product.

stem: For product liability to apply, the injury or damage must occur off the business premises, with an exception for:
explanation: To be covered under product liability, the injury or damage must occur off the business premises except for restaurants, and the product must be under the total control of the customer.

stem: Completed operations coverage applies when:
options: The work is still in progress at the time of the occurrence
The injury occurs on the insured's premises
The insured has completed the project and left before the occurrence, and it is always an off-premises exposure
The product is still under the insured's control
explanation: Completed operations covers defective workmanship and designs causing injury or damages in the future, and the insured must have completed the project and left before the occurrence; completed operations are always an off-premises exposure.

stem: On a claims made form:
options: The occurrence may occur at any time and the claim during the policy period
The occurrence must occur during the policy period and the claim may be made at any time in the future
Both the occurrence and the claim may occur at any time
The occurrence must occur during the policy period and the claim must be made during the policy period
explanation: On a claims made form the occurrence must occur during the policy period and the claim must be made during the policy period, while an occurrence form allows the claim to be made at any time in the future.

stem: On the claims made form, if the insured reports occurrences that took place during the policy period within the basic 60-day reporting period, there is an extended reporting period of:
options: 5 years for all claims of any kind
5 years for claims resulting from those reported occurrences only
Unlimited time for those occurrences only
explanation: If the insured reports occurrences that took place during the policy period within the 60-day period, there will be an extended reporting period of 5 years for claims resulting from those reported occurrences only.

stem: The commercial package policy is described as:
options: An identical form to the businessowners policy
A customizable package policy for larger businesses
A policy restricted to financial institutions
explanation: The commercial package policy is a customizable package policy, not a package policy in the BOP sense, and it is designed for larger businesses.

stem: Under the commercial policy declarations, the first name listed has:
explanation: The declarations note that the first name listed has the first named insured duties, and the first named insured may cancel, make changes, and receives the bill and premium refund.

stem: Which coverage part provides coverage for valuable papers and records?
explanation: The commercial inland marine coverage part lists accounts receivable, commercial articles, contractors equipment floater, electronic data processing, installation floater, signs, and valuable papers and records.

stem: Inland marine insurance is almost always written on what basis?
options: An actual cash value only basis
explanation: Inland marine is property insurance on certain kinds of property and is almost always written on a special form basis.

stem: Which property cannot be insured using inland marine policies and forms?
options: Real property and the contents of the building
explanation: Real property and contents of the building cannot be insured using inland marine policies and forms, and businesses personal property is not covered when it is more than 100 feet from the premises whether in a truck or not.

stem: Bailee's customer coverage under inland marine is designed for:
options: Real property owned by the business
Money and securities in a vault
Items in the care, custody and control of the business, such as a dry cleaner's customers' clothing
explanation: Bailee's customer coverage is for items in the care, custody and control of the business, such as dry cleaners.

stem: Burglary is defined as the taking of property:
options: With evidence of forced entry into or out of a premises or safe, after hours with no people present
By causing or threatening bodily harm during business hours
Without any evidence that a crime occurred
explanation: Burglary is the taking of property with evidence of forced entry into or out of a premises or safe, after hours with no people present.

stem: Robbery is defined as the taking of property:
options: With evidence of forced entry after hours
By a messenger outside the premises
By causing or threatening bodily harm, during hours with people present
Without evidence that a crime occurred
explanation: Robbery is the taking of property by causing or threatening bodily harm, during hours with people present.

stem: The manual calls which coverage the best crime coverage?
explanation: Theft, defined as any act of stealing, is described in the manual as the best crime coverage.

stem: A watchperson is excluded from the definition of custodian, and mysterious disappearance means:
options: Property was taken by force during business hours
Property was taken by an employee
Property is missing but there is no evidence that a crime has occurred
explanation: A custodian excludes any person acting as watchperson or janitor, while mysterious disappearance means property is missing but there is no evidence that a crime has occurred.
